findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving the service user near-administrative control over compute, storage, and serverless resources in the account. Compromise of this user's credentials would allow data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and arbitrary EC2/Lambda execution.

A permanent IAM access key is created for the user with no PGP key specified, so the secret is stored in plaintext in Terraform state. Long-lived static keys attached to a highly privileged user are a prime credential-theft target and should be replaced with IAM roles / STS short-lived credentials.
No pgp_key is configured, so the access key secret is written unencrypted to the Terraform state file; the referenced encrypted_secret attribute will be empty/null without it.

Outputting access key material (aws_iam_access_key.svc_deploy_key.encrypted_secret) exposes the credential through terraform output and the state file; the output is not marked sensitive, so it can be printed to CI logs.
A long-lived IAM user with broad wildcard permissions is created with no MFA enforcement or permissions boundary, relying solely on static access keys for authentication.
